findings.title: Portuguese component names violate language policy
findings.impact: CLAUDE.md Hard rule violation: 'Code, identifiers, comments, commit messages, documentation, config are English only.' Component names and identifiers in Portuguese make the codebase inconsistent and harder to maintain across a distributed team. These are interface definitions and exports, not user-facing content.
findings.correction: Rename components to English: Experiencia → Experience, Habilidades → Skills, CardExperiencia → ExperienceCard, Entrada → Entry
findings.verification: Run typecheck and tests after rename; audit imports across all files for references; check e2e tests for accessibility assertions on the renamed components

findings.title: GithubIcon component uses 'Github' instead of 'GitHub'
findings.impact: Proper noun 'GitHub' is capitalized incorrectly in component naming. This appears in both apps (portfolio & blog). All visible user-facing aria-labels correctly say 'GitHub', but the component name is mislabeled, inconsistent with the brand name and the cspell dictionary.
findings.correction: Rename GithubIcon component files and exports to GitHubIcon across both apps. Update all imports in Footer.tsx and Contact.tsx in both apps.
findings.verification: Grep for 'GithubIcon' should return zero results; verify Footer and Contact components render correctly in e2e tests

findings.title: Inconsistent TypeScript capitalization in skills.ts
findings.impact: Variable name 'siTypescript' (from simple-icons) is a library-provided identifier and cannot be changed. However, this is not a finding in user content. TypeScript is universally written 'TypeScript' with capital S and T — this is the official spelling. The display name (line 44) is correct.
findings.correction: No correction needed — the import name is from an external library (simple-icons). The display name is already correct ('TypeScript'). This is not a violation, cspell flagged a library export name.
findings.verification: Verify cspell can be configured to exclude library-generated identifiers, or add 'siTypescript' to the project dictionary if needed for CI

findings.title: Front-end capitalization variant: 'Front-end' is canonical
findings.impact: Grep shows 11 occurrences of 'Front-end' (with hyphen) vs 0 of 'frontend' (no hyphen) and 0 of 'front end' (two words). This is consistent. Canonical form is 'Front-end' with hyphen.
findings.correction: No correction needed — variant is consistent throughout the project.
findings.verification: Grep confirms zero deviations from 'Front-end' format

findings.title: Duplicate theme toggle logic in portfolio and blog

references: CLAUDE.md Standing decisions #1: 'useTheme.ts / ThemeToggle.tsx are duplicated in both apps. Known and accepted.'

findings.impact: CLAUDE.md explicitly states this is deliberate (extract-on-second-use rule: code moves to packages/ only after a *second* app actually needs it). Not a violation, but noted for completeness.
findings.correction: No correction needed — this is a standing decision, not a defect.
findings.verification: Confirm both implementations are byte-identical or have intentional, documented differences

unverified_hypotheses: Portuguese words in e2e test files (Sobre, Construindo, sistemas, escalam) appear only in test assertions checking translated UI output — these are legitimate and do not violate the language policy for code/identifiers. Confirmed by inspection of test files: they are string literals being compared against translated UI, not identifiers or comments.
